name: Article 50: Transparency obligations for providers and deployers of certain AI systems
summary: Providers must tell people they are interacting with AI and mark synthetic content in a machine-readable format; deployers must disclose emotion recognition, biometric categorisation, deep fakes and AI-generated public-interest text.

title.v: Transparency obligations for providers and deployers of certain AI systems

chapter.v: Chapter IV, Transparency obligations for providers and deployers of certain AI systems

interaction.v: Providers design AI systems that interact directly with natural persons so that the persons are informed that they are interacting with an AI system, unless this is obvious to a reasonably well-informed, observant and circumspect person.

marking.v: Providers of AI systems, including general-purpose AI systems, that generate synthetic audio, image, video or text ensure that the outputs are marked in a machine-readable format and detectable as artificially generated or manipulated.

emotion_biometric.v: Deployers of an emotion recognition or biometric categorisation system inform the natural persons exposed to it of its operation.

deep_fake.v: Deployers of an AI system that generates or manipulates image, audio or video content constituting a deep fake disclose that the content is artificially generated or manipulated; for evidently artistic, creative, satirical or fictional works the disclosure is limited to the existence of such content.

public_interest_text.v: Deployers of an AI system that generates or manipulates text published to inform the public on matters of public interest disclose that the text is artificially generated or manipulated, unless it has undergone human review or editorial control under a person's editorial responsibility.

timing.v: The information is given in a clear and distinguishable manner at the latest at the time of the first interaction or exposure, and conforms to the applicable accessibility requirements.

exceptions.v: Paragraphs 1 to 4 do not apply, with conditions that differ by paragraph, to uses authorised by law to detect, prevent, investigate or prosecute criminal offences; paragraph 2 also does not apply to assistive functions for standard editing or to systems that do not substantially alter the input data or its semantics.

codes_of_practice.v: The Commission encourages codes of practice at Union level on the detection, marking and labelling of generated or manipulated content, assesses their adequacy for paragraphs 2 and 4 under the procedure of Article 56(6), and may adopt an implementing act with common rules if it deems a code inadequate.

general.note: Chapter IV is not among the exceptions of Article 113, points (a) to (d).

existing_generative_systems.note: For providers of systems that generate synthetic audio, image, video or text and were placed on the market before 2 August 2026, the date by which they comply with Article 50(2).

amended_by.note: Replaces paragraph 7: the Commission, not the AI Office, encourages the codes of practice, which now also cover marking, and assesses their adequacy instead of approving them by implementing act.
